farraa:1-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ﴾. So when a man wants to divorce his wife for the ʿidda (waiting period), he should wait until she has one menstrual period, then divorce her; when she has a menstrual period after the divorce, he divorces her again; and if she has a period after the two divorces, he divorces her a third time. This is divorce for the ʿidda; she is then irrevocably separated from him and is not lawful for him until she marries another husband.
Divorce according to the Sunna is that he divorces her while she is in a state of purity in which there has been no intercourse, then leaves her until she has had three menstrual periods. If he does that, she is separated from him, and marrying her is not lawful for him except with a new dowry, and he has no right to take her back.
His saying: ﴿وَأَحْصُواْ ٱلْعِدَّةَ﴾: [i.e.] the menstrual periods.
His saying: ﴿لاَ تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِن بُيُوتِهِنَّ﴾.
[That is,] those in which they were divorced; and they are not to go out of their own accord ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ﴾. Some said: except that they commit an indecency [— except that she commits an offence liable to a ḥadd punishment, so that she is brought out for it to be carried out on her. And some said: except that they commit an indecency] — except that they disobey and go out, for her going out is a manifest indecency.
His saying: ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾.
He is saying: [keep them] in the remaining divorce on fair terms, or release them on fair terms. He said: and "fair terms" (maʿrūf) means kindness.
His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَمْراً﴾.
This is the taking back [of the wife] in the two divorces.
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾.
When she has a period after the two divorces, up until she has the third and has not yet bathed, he may take her back as long as she has not bathed from the third period.

farraa:10-11.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْراً﴾ ﴿رَّسُولاً﴾.
It came down in the Book with رسول in the accusative, and that is the [proper] Arabic way. Had it been رسولٌ in the nominative, it would be correct, because ذكرا is the end of a verse, and starting afresh (istiʾnāf) after verse-ends is good. Similar to it is His saying: "التائبون", preceded by: ﴿إِنَّ اللهَ اشْتَرَى مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾; when He said: ﴿وذلك هو الفوزُ العظيمُ﴾, a fresh start was made with the nominative. Similar to it: ﴿وتَرَكَهُمْ فى ظُلُمَاتٍ لا يُبْصِِرُونَ، صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ﴾. And similar to it: ﴿ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ﴾, then He said: ﴿فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُريدُ﴾, which is an indefinite word describing a definite one, so a fresh start was made with the nominative, because it comes after a verse-end.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَمِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ﴾.
[I.e.] He created seven [and created of the earth the like of them]. Had it been read "مثلُهن" [in the nominative], since the verb is not overtly expressed, it would be correct.
You say in speech: رأيت لأخيك إبلا، ولوالدك شاء كثير (I saw camels belonging to your brother, and your father has many sheep), when the verb is not expressed [with the second].
He said: He means that with the latter [noun], the nominative and the accusative are both permissible when the latter has an adjective that takes the nominative; so draw analogies from it, if Allah wills.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ﴾.
The readers all read it with tanwīn [بالغٌ أمرَه]. Had it been read: بالغ أمرِه [in the genitive construct], it would be correct; and had it been read: بالغٌ أمرُه with the nominative, it would be permissible.
[Translator's note: the lemma in the printed text appears in the genitive-construct form, while the comment states that all readers read it with tanwīn.]

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: [200/b] ﴿وَٱللاَّئِي يَئِسْنَ مِنَ ٱلْمَحِيضِ مِن نِّسَآئِكُمْ إِنِ ٱرْتَبْتُمْ﴾.
He is saying: if you are in doubt and do not know what her waiting period is. They mention that Muʿādh ibn Jabal asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: We know the waiting period of the woman who menstruates; what is the waiting period of the old woman who has despaired [of menstruation]? Then there came down: ﴿ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاَثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ﴾. A man stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah! What is the waiting period of the young girl who has not menstruated? He said: "And those who have not menstruated" are like the old woman who has despaired: her waiting period is three months. Another stood up and said: And the pregnant women, what is their waiting period? Then there came down: ﴿وَأُوْلاَتُ ٱلأَحْمَالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَن يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ﴾. So when the pregnant woman gives birth to what is in her womb she becomes lawful for husbands, even if her dead husband is still on the bier, not yet buried.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿مِّن وُجْدِكُمْ﴾.
He is saying: according to what each of you can afford. If he is well-off, he provides amply for her in housing and maintenance; and if he is in straitened means, then according to that. Then He said: ﴿وَإِن كُنَّ أُوْلاَتِ حَمْلٍ فَأَنفِقُواْ عَلَيْهِنَّ حَتَّىٰ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ﴾: he spends on her from the share of what is in her womb. Then He said: ﴿فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾: the wage for nursing.
His saying: ﴿وَأْتَمِرُواْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾.
He is saying: let the woman not harm her husband, and let him not harm her. The readers have agreed on ḍamma on the واو of "وُجْدكم" and on ḍamma on the قاف of "قُدِر" [and on reading it light]; had they read قُدِّر it would be correct.
And had they read مِنْ "وَجْدِكم" it would be correct, because it is the dialect of Banū Tamīm.

farraa:8-9.t:
His saying: ﴿فَحَاسَبْنَاهَا حِسَاباً شَدِيداً﴾.
In the Hereafter, ﴿وَعَذَّبْنَاهَا عَذَاباً نُّكْراً﴾ in this world; it is [a case of] what is put first and what is put last (muqaddam wa-muʾakhkhar). Then He said: ﴿فَذَاقَتْ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهَا﴾ of the punishment of this world, ﴿وَكَانَ عَاقِبَةُ أَمْرِهَا خُسْراً﴾: the Fire and its punishment.
